name: core
summary: Commonly used commands for basic browser interaction.

commands.name: back
commands.description: Navigate back in the current tab's history.

commands.name: click
commands.description:
Click on HTML element(s) matches by selector.  If multiple is true, then all
elements matched by selector will be clicked in the order they are returned.
Otherwise, an error is returned unless selector matches exactly one element.

#### Examples

##### Click on the element with id "login"
```
click "#login"
```

##### Click on all `<a>` elements on the page, waiting 150ms between each click.
```

	click "a" {
	  multiple: true,
	  delay:    "150ms",
	}

```

options.name: count
options.description: Number of clicks to perform.

options.name: delay
options.description: Time to waith between mousedown and mouseup events.

options.name: button
options.description: Which mouse button to simulate during click. Values are "left", "right", "middle". Default "left".

options.name: match_text
options.description: If provided, this represents a regular expression that the text value of matching elements must match to be clicked.

commands.name: click_at
commands.description: Click the page at the given X, Y coordinates.

options.name: x
options.description: The X-coordinate to click at

options.name: y
options.description: The Y-coordinate to click at

options.name: steps
options.description: Number of steps to interpolate when moving.

commands.name: env
commands.description:
Retrieves a system environment variable and returns the value of it, or a
fallback value if the variable does not exist or (optionally) is empty.

#### Examples

##### Get the value of the `USER` environment variable and store it
```
env 'USER' -> $user
```

##### Require the `LANG`, `USER`, and `CI` environment variables; and fail they are not set.
```
env 'LANG' { required: true }
env 'USER' { required: true }
env 'CI'   { required: true }
```

options.name: fallback
options.description:
The value to return if the environment variable does not exist, or
(optionally) is empty.

options.name: required
options.description: Whether empty values should be ignored or not.

options.name: detect_type
options.description: Whether automatic type detection should be performed or not.

options.name: joiner
options.description:
If specified, this string will be used to split matching values into a
list of values. This is useful for environment variables that contain
multiple values joined by a separator (e.g: the PATH variable.)

commands.name: exit
commands.description: Immediately close the browser without error or delay.

commands.name: export

commands.name: fail
commands.description: Immediately exit the script in an error-like fashion with a specific message.

commands.name: focus
commands.description: Focuses the given HTML element described by selector. One and only one element may match the selector.

options.name: timeout

commands.name: forward
commands.description: Navigate forward in the current tab's history.

commands.name: go
commands.description:
Navigate to a URL.

#### Examples

##### Go to Google.
```
go "google.com"
```

##### Go to www.example.com, only wait for the first network response, and don't fail if the request times out.
```

	go "https://www.example.com" {
	  timeout:             '10s',
	  continue_on_timeout: true,
	  load_event_name:     'Network.responseReceived',
	}

```

options.name: referrer
options.description:
If a URL is specified, it will be used as the HTTP Referer [sic] header
field when going to the given page. If the URL of the currently-loaded
page and the referrer are the same, the page will no change.

For this reason, you may specify the special value 'random', which will
generate a URL with a randomly generated path component to ensure that
it is always different from the current page. Specifying None will omit
the field from the request.

options.name: wait_for_load
options.description: Whether to block until the page has finished loading.

options.name: timeout
options.description: The amount of time to wait for the page to load.

options.name: clear_requests
options.description:
Whether the resources stack that is queried in page::resources and
page::resource is cleared before navigating. Set this to false to
preserve the ability to retrieve data that was loaded on previous pages.

options.name: require_originating_request
options.description:
Whether the originating network request is required in the return value.  If this is
false, the response may be missing status, headers, and timing details.

options.name: continue_on_error
options.description:
Whether to continue execution if an error is encountered during page
load (e.g.: HTTP 4xx/5xx, SSL, TCP connection errors).

options.name: continue_statuses
options.description: These HTTP status codes are not considered errors.

options.name: load_event_name
options.description: The RPC event to wait for before proceeding to the next command.

options.name: username
options.description: Provide a username if one is requested via HTTP Basic authentication.

options.name: password
options.description: Provide a password if one is requested via HTTP Basic authentication.

options.name: realm
options.description: Only provide credentials if the HTTP Basic Authentication Realm matches this one.

commands.name: run
commands.description:
Evaluates another Friendscript loaded from another file. The filename is the
absolute path or basename of the file to search for in the FRIENDSCRIPT_PATH
environment variable to load and evaluate. The FRIENDSCRIPT_PATH variable
behaves like the the traditional *nix PATH variable, wherein multiple paths
can be specified as a colon-separated (:) list. The directory of the calling
script (if available) will always be checked first.

Returns: The value of the variable named by result_key at the end of the
evaluated script's execution.

commands.name: type
commands.description:
Input the given textual data as keyboard input into the currently focused
page element.  The input text contains raw unicode characters that will be typed
literally, as well as key names (in accordance with the DOM pre-defined keynames
described at https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/KeyboardEvent/key/Key_Values).
These sequences appear between square brackets "[" "]".

Example: Type in the Konami code

	type "[ArrowUp][ArrowUp][ArrowDown][ArrowDown][ArrowLeft][ArrowRight][ArrowLeft][ArrowRight]BA"

name: page
summary: Commands for inspecting and manipulating the current DOM document and browser viewport.

commands.name: pdf
commands.description:
Render the current page as a PDF document, writing it to the given filename or writable
destination object.

options.name: autoclose
options.description: Whether the given destination should be automatically closed for writing after the PDF is written.

options.name: format
options.description: Paper format of the PDF pages

options.name: landscape
options.description: Orient the PDF in landscape.

options.name: scale
options.description: Scale of the rendered page. Between [0.1, 2.0], default is 1.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The filesystem path that the screenshot was written to.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The size of the screenshot (in bytes).

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Remove all occurrences of the element(s) matching the given selector.

commands.name: screenshot
commands.description:
Render the current page as a PNG or JPEG image, writing it to the given filename or writable
destination object.

If the filename is the string `"temporary"`, a file will be created in the system's
temporary area (e.g.: `/tmp`) and the screenshot will be written there.  It is the caller's
responsibility to remove the temporary file if desired.  The temporary file path is available in
the return object's `path` parameter.

options.name: format
options.description: The output image format of the screenshot.  Valid options are "png" or "jpeg".

options.name: quality
options.description: The quality of the image used during encoding.  Only applies to "jpeg" format.

options.name: autoclose
options.description:
Whether the given destination should be automatically closed for writing after the
screenshot is written.

options.name: autoresize
options.description: Automatically resize the screen to the width and height.

options.name: style
options.description: A stylesheet to apply while taking the screenshot.

options.name: omit_background
options.description: Hide the default page background to produce transparent screenshots.

options.name: allow_animations
options.description: Disable CSS animations and transitions when taking the screenshot.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: The width of the screenshot (in pixels).

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: The height of the screenshot (in pixels).

parameters.name: x
parameters.description: The X position (relative to the viewport) the screenshot was taken at.

parameters.name: y
parameters.description: The Y position (relative to the viewport) the screenshot was taken at.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The filesystem path that the screenshot was written to.

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: The size of the screenshot (in bytes).

commands.name: source
commands.description: Return the source for the given element, or for the whole page.

commands.name: text
commands.description: Return the text content for the given element, or for the whole page.

commands.name: json
commands.description: Parses the given file as a JSON document and returns the resulting value.

commands.name: yaml
commands.description: Parses the given file as a YAML document and returns the resulting value.

commands.name: encode_query
commands.description:
Take a map or previous URL response structure and encode the values into a string
that can be used in another URL or form post data.  This command does not automaticlly
prepend a "?" character to the output.

commands.name: escape
commands.description: Escapes the string so it can be safely placed inside a URL path segment, replacing special characters (including /) with %XX sequences as needed.

commands.name: parse
commands.description: Parse the given URL string or structure, and return a structured representation of the various parts of a URL.

commands.name: parse_query
commands.description: Take a URL or map of query string key=value pairs and return a map of values.

commands.name: clear
commands.description: Unset the value at the given key.

commands.name: ensure
commands.description: Emit an error if the given key does not exist, optionally with a user-specified message.

commands.name: get
commands.description: Return the value of a specific variable defined in a scope.

commands.name: interpolate
commands.description: Return a value interpolated with values from a scope or ones that are explicitly provided.

commands.name: keys
commands.description: Return a sorted list of all variable names in the current scope.

commands.name: pop
commands.description:
Take the last value from the array at key.  If key is an array, the last value of
that array will be returned and the remainder will be left at key.  Empty arrays will
return nil and be unset.  Non-array values will be returned and the key will be unset.

commands.name: push
commands.description:
Push the given value onto the array at the specified key, creating the array if not
present, and converting the existing value into an array already set to non-array value.

commands.name: set
commands.description:
Set the named variable to the given value, optionally interpolating variables from the current
scope into the variable.

name: xml
summary: Commands for interacting with XML documents

commands.name: query
commands.description: List all cookies, either for the given set of URLs or for the current tab (if omitted).

options.name: xpath
options.description: Return a list of nodes matching the given XPath expression.
